title: Fix ES module directory import in @object-ui/core
body:
## Fix ES Module Directory Import Error in @object-ui/core

### Problem
Two test files were failing in CI with `Directory import is not supported resolving ES modules` when importing from `@object-ui/core/dist/types`.

### Root Cause Analysis
The real issue was that `packages/core/src/types/index.ts` contains ONLY TypeScript interfaces (type-only declarations), which are erased at compile time and don't generate any JavaScript output. 

When the code had `export * from './types/index.js'`, TypeScript would copy this to the output, but at runtime Node.js couldn't find `dist/types/index.js` because it was never generated.

When changed to `export * from './types'`, Node.js tried to import from the `types` directory, which is not allowed in ES modules.

### Solution
Use `export type *` for type-only exports. This tells TypeScript to only export the types (for type-checking) without creating a runtime module dependency.

```typescript
// Before (causes runtime error - file doesn't exist)
export * from './types/index.js';

// My first attempt (causes directory import error)  
export * from './types';

// Correct solution (type-only export, no runtime dependency)
export type * from './types';
```

### Changes
- `packages/core/src/index.ts`: Changed line 9 to use `export type *` for the types directory

### Testing
- ✅ Built all packages successfully
- ✅ Both previously failing test files now pass  
- ✅ All other tests continue to pass
- ✅ Types are still exported and available for import in other packages
- ✅ Code review completed with no issues
- ✅ Security scan completed with no vulnerabilities

### Summary
The fix correctly addresses the ES module directory import error by using TypeScript's `export type *` syntax for type-only exports, which avoids creating runtime module dependencies while still making the types available for type-checking.
